preset.description: A saw-based spectrum with a gentle Tilt, a touch of Stretch and a slow Chorus makes a wide, glassy pad. Try pulling Tilt down for a duller tone, or raising Chorus and Width.
A square spectrum with Odd/Even pushed to the odd side gives a hollow, woody reed. A slow LFO sweeps Odd/Even toward the even partials so the tone keeps turning from hollow to bright.

Stretch spreads the partials out of tune with each other and Decay lets each one ring and die on a trigger, so every note strikes like a struck bell. Change Stretch toward negative values for a softer, gong-like cluster.

A low saw drone whose partials are notched by a Comb: a slow LFO on Comb Phase moves the notches up the spectrum, so the drone sweeps like a phaser made purely of harmonics. Try Comb Spacing for different notch patterns.

A short rhythmic pluck whose Partials count and Tilt are pushed around by a random generator, so every note is a different slice of the spectrum, from a pure sine to a rich buzz. Lower Damp for brighter plucks.

Two 10 kHz carriers beat against each other; a slow LFO sweeps Beat from a pulse to a whistle and back, and the detector plucks only the difference tone. Try the Mixer setting (Diode or Overdriven) for a buzzier beat, or raise Drift.

With Pull up, the two carriers hold each other near lock, so the beat does not run steadily: it lurches in single sub-bass blips that bunch up and stall as Drift pushes the pair across the lock edge. Try nudging Beat or Drift.

The Lock output is a gate: it goes high whenever the carriers pull into step. A slow wobble on Detune drives the pair in and out of lock, and a melody is only allowed to play while it is locked. Change Pull or Detune Range to change how often it happens.

Low carriers with the Detector opened let the sum tone whistle on top of the beat, and Warm-up makes both start flat and slide into tune while the transport runs. The Overdriven mixer turns the beat into a soft triangle. Try Detector at 0 to hear the whistle vanish.

A sequencer drives Pitch, transposing both carriers so the difference tone plays the tune. The Beat output measures that tone and feeds an oscillator an octave up, so a second voice follows the heterodyne melody. Try Mixer Diode for more bite.

A drum loop and riff pass through Bender at 1/16 with a low Chance: now and then a slice repeats twice and stutters before the groove carries on. Raise Chance for more, or Repeats for longer stutters.
An arpeggio goes through Bender at 1/8 with Slice at 40 %: repeated fragments cut into ratchets while Chance picks which beats get them. Change Seed to hear another set of decisions.

A slow chord pad is re-pitched downward in Smear mode with Bend at one half and some Bend Var: pieces of the sound sag and slur like a tape machine losing speed. Try Bend Steps on Free for a continuous slide.

Mode Shuffle with Chance at 70 %, Corrupt at 80 % and a little Slice cuts a beat and bass line into constantly rearranged, crumbling pieces. Pull Chance down to keep the groove, or try Fold and Dropout modes.

Chance is zero, so Bender stays clean until a sequencer's trigger hits the Glitch input: only those steps are Folded, and the Random output jumps a filter's cutoff along with each decision. Change the sequencer steps to move the glitches.

A 4 × 3 corner of the grid in F Lydian: X runs every 16th, Y steps down a row at the end of each pass, so a twelve-step figure of bright broken chords turns against the bar. Change Columns, Rows or a cell's pitch and the figure follows.

Eight columns by two rows of E minor bass under a four-on-the-floor beat. The Mod value of every cell opens the filter, so each row has its own brightness: edit the Mod column of a cell to change the accent.

Cartesian mode: no clocks, two slow LFOs steer the crosshair across a full 8 × 8 grid of minor pentatonic notes, and a note sounds whenever the crosshair enters a new cell. Move X and Y by hand or change the LFO rates to wander faster or slower.

X moves back and forth across five columns on the 8ths while Y steps a row every dotted quarter: the marimba line takes ages to repeat and never lines up with the beat. Row End ticks a hat and Grid End thumps a kick; try other Y Rate values.

Both playheads move at random, so the Hirajoshi arpeggio hops around the grid in a fixed but never-obvious order (the Seed decides it). Mod swings the filter and a slow LFO lifts the whole cutoff; change Seed or the directions to deal a new tune.

An envelope that follows a bass line is drawn by a slow pen with little damping, so the pen overshoots and wobbles around each level: that wobble sweeps the filter. Turn Writing Speed up for a tight envelope, Damping up for a lazy one, and watch the pen on the paper.

A smooth slow LFO is drawn with a pen that sticks: it only moves once the change has built up, so Pen becomes irregular little steps that a Quantizer turns into a wandering pentatonic melody. Lower Friction for a smoother line and more notes, raise it for fewer, bigger leaps.

A smooth random walk is drawn live on a four-bar strip: one voice plays the live pen, and a second plays what the paper replays backwards, so the melody answers itself in reverse. Try Replay Speed 0.5 or 2, or switch Interpolation to Step.

The drum bus is drawn as a level trace (Log dB, Response 100 ms), and an inverted Pen pumps a chord pad so it ducks on every kick. Change Detector or Response, or use the Replay output for a duck that arrives a loop later.

A curve drawn on the paper is read as a table: Replay Speed is 0 and a slow LFO on Offset scrubs through it, so the drawn shape becomes a looping melody. Draw on the paper in the view (Shift-drag for lines), or set Interpolation to Step to hear each plateau.

A slow bass line plays the root and Chord Osc stacks a Minor 7 on it, spread with the Open voicing, a little Detune and Stereo, and Glide so each chord melts into the next. Try other Chord types, or Inversion for different voice leading.

In Scale mode a plain melody becomes a chord progression: each note of the tune turns into the diatonic triad on that scale degree, changing exactly on the step through Latch. Change Root or Scale and the whole harmony follows.

The four Pitch outputs carry the chord's tones; a Switch steps through them on every sixteenth and plays an oscillator, so the arpeggio follows whatever chord Chord Osc is holding, while the full chord hums underneath. Change Chord or Voicing to re-voice the arpeggio.

Short dominant-ninth stabs on the off-beats, voiced Drop 2 with a squarer Shape and a snappy envelope, over a four-on-the-floor beat. Try Dominant 7, Quartal or a higher Inversion for a different punch.

Pure sine voices stacked in fourths, with a low oscillator in the FM input and FM Depth moved by a slow LFO: the chord shimmers between smooth and metallic. Turn Detune and Stereo up for a wider glow.

A bar-long sequence of single notes becomes a lush A minor pad. Voice Leading on Smooth + Top picks the inversion that moves least, so the top voice glides and the chords flow instead of jumping. Try Voice Leading Off to hear the raw jumps, or Voicing Close.

Plucked quarter notes in D Dorian each become an open-voiced ninth chord that is strummed across the four voices instead of arriving at once, with an echo behind it. Turn Strum up for a lazier roll, or change Strum Order to Down.

Syncopated single notes turn into short minor-seventh stabs over a root-note bass, on a broken beat. In Chromatic mode the Chord knob picks the quality: try Dominant 7, Minor add9 or Sus4, and raise Inversion for a higher voicing.

Mode Follow: the chord is whatever the Harmony Master's progression says (A minor 7, F, C, G), voiced as a drop-2 pad with a root bass below. A slow LFO into Pitch lifts and drops the register. Change Voicing or Anchor in the module's view.

A wandering Random feeds Pitch; in a whole-tone scale every triad is an augmented chord, so the harmony floats without a home. An LFO gates the chords as eighth-note pulses. Switch Scale to Hirajoshi or Blues in the view for a different colour.

patches.name: Coin Toss: Heads or Tails Drums

preset.description: A steady sixteenth-note gate is tossed twice: channel 1 sends each step to a closed hat or a quiet snare ghost note, channel 2 (with some Memory, so it comes in runs) occasionally turns it into an open hat. The kick and backbeat stay fixed, the rest never repeats. Move Probability 1 and 2.

One pentatonic melody is dealt note by note to two different instruments: a round low pluck on A and a bright high one on B, panned apart. Memory makes them trade in runs instead of strictly alternating. Raise Memory 1 for longer runs, move Probability 1 towards one side.

Both channels are in Latch mode, so A and B are always opposite. Channel 1 tosses once a bar and decides whether the pad or the arpeggio is muted; channel 2 independently switches the drums on or off. The song re-arranges itself. Change Mode to Trigger or Toggle, or the Seed.

Link is Shared and Loop is 16 tosses: one coin decides a nested pattern, a 30 % clap and a 70 % closed hat that always contains it, and the whole random figure repeats every bar over a steady kick and bass. Change the Seed for another groove, or Loop to Off to let it wander.

patches.name: Coin Toss: Coin on the Pitch

preset.description: The Coin outputs are control voltages: channel 1 in Toggle mode occasionally flips a switch that lifts a bell melody up a fifth, channel 2 in Latch mode opens or closes a low-pass filter on a drone with each toss. Nothing is gated; the coin steers the sound. Change Probability 1 to flip more often.

Six taps in a Ring feed each other with a dark, tape-like Character, so single soft notes smear into a slowly turning pad. Move Scatter and Width to change where the taps sit, or Routing to Chain to hear a straighter line.

With Sync on a dotted eighth and Parallel routing, four taps place echoes on a rhythmic grid around a short plucked tune; Scatter nudges them off it. Try Taps, Scatter and Feedback for denser or sparser patterns.

In Mesh routing every line feeds every other, and Reverse plays part of the echoes backwards, so each note blooms into swelling, reversed clouds. Raise Jitter to blur the timing further; Time Change decides if time moves bend the pitch.
A drum beat goes through a Chain of lines locked to the tempo; Jitter and Scatter make the repeats a loose, dubby shadow of the groove. Pull Mix down for a subtle effect or up for a wall of echoes.

Feedback is almost at its limit, so the network sustains into a self-holding drone around a sparse bass line; a slow LFO on Character shifts it from clean to gritty. Lower Feedback to hear it settle, or push it past 100 %.

In the straight corner of the map (low X, low Y) the Drum Map plays a steady kick on every beat, a backbeat snare and eighth-note hats, under a pulsing bass. Move X toward broken or Y toward busy, or turn the Density knobs to thin and fill each drum.

A slow LFO on X and a seeded Random on Y make the beat travel the whole map, from straight to broken and from sparse to busy, with Chaos adding ghost notes that come back identically every time. Try replacing the LFO with your own X and Y moves.

A square LFO pulses the Fill gate for one bar in every four, adding Fill Amount to every Density so extra kicks, snares and sixteenth hats appear before the loop turns round. Raise Fill Amount for bigger fills, or make the LFO faster for constant fills.

Rate 1/8 stretches the two-bar map to four bars and X sits at the half-time edge: a sparse kick, a heavy snare on beat 3 and a few hats. The snare and hats feed a long delay through the mixer sends. Try Swing and Chaos for a looser feel.

Rate 1/16T and a high Swing give a rolling shuffle, and Chaos at 60 % with a fresh nudge every bar keeps adding and dropping ghost notes around the steady backbone. Turn Chaos down for a rigid groove or set Chaos Rate to Frozen to fix one version.
A saw pad runs through two band-pass filters in parallel, a formant pair that a slow LFO on Spread slides between vowels. Try Res 1 and Res 2 for a sharper or breathier voice.
A growly saw bass in Serial with a high-pass on filter 1 and a low-pass on filter 2: a band whose width is Spread and whose position is Cutoff. A beat keeps time; try Spread and Drive.

One mono arpeggio goes in on the left; in Stereo routing each filter takes a channel and Spread places their cutoffs apart, so an LFO on Spread makes the image breathe left and right. Change Resonance for more ring.
Parallel with the second filter inverted turns two band-passes into a steep notch. It sweeps through a bright saw riff over a beat; Spread widens the hole in the sound.

With Link on Mirror, one slow LFO on Mode 1 morphs the pair from two low-passes through band-pass to two notches, mirrored on the other filter, while Saturating Character adds bite. Sweep Mode 1 and Mode 2 by hand.

Oscillator B hard-syncs oscillator A and a slow LFO sweeps Tune B, so the lead's tone rips from mellow to searing and back. Change Sync for a softer or harder grip, or pull Tune B to a fixed value to freeze the sound.

Sine B frequency-modulates sine A at an odd ratio (B Tune +7 semitones) with Exponential FM, and a decaying envelope on both level and FM turns every note into a struck, clangorous bell. Try changing Tune B for different metals.
A triangle bass pushed through the stereo wavefolder: an envelope opens Fold on every note so each one starts snarling and settles into a round tone. Raise Symmetry for a more even-harmonic growl.
Two saw cores a few cents apart with strong Drift and wide stereo Width: the slowly beating pair makes a warm, breathing pad. Raise Fine B or Drift for a wider, less stable sound.

The Ring output multiplies the two cores into inharmonic clangs; a short envelope turns it into a metallic percussion line over a light beat. Change Tune B to retune the clang, or Octave B for a lower rumble.
A drum beat feeds the Sidechain while a saw chord sits on the input: with Vocode at 100 % and Env From on Sidechain, the ten bands let the beat's spectrum speak through the chord. Try Release and Q.
Width narrows the bank to a two-band window and a slow LFO on Scan moves it across the spectrum, so a held saw chord sweeps like a gentle formant filter. Open Width back up to hear the full sound.

With Tuning on Harmonic and a high Q the ten bands ring at a note's harmonics: noise bursts and a beat become pitched hits that follow a sequencer into the Pitch input. Change Tuning to Scale or lower Q.
An LFO on Shift slides all ten bands up and down together with a modest Q, giving an arpeggio a vocal, phaser-like sweep. Raise Q for more whistle, or Spacing to change how far apart the bands sit.

Stereo is set to Odd/Even split, so a mono saw pad leaves the odd bands on the left and the even bands on the right: a wide, hollow image. A slow LFO on Odd/Even moves the emphasis between them; try Tilt.

A slow triangle LFO sweeps Formant up and down over a simple tune, so the resonant peak wanders through the harmonics like a hand on a wah pedal. Try Narrow for a sharper peak, or Body for a fuller base.

An envelope snaps Formant upward on every bass note and lets it fall, giving the squelch of a resonant filter without any filter. Raise Narrow for more bite and shorten the envelope for a tighter pluck.
A slow chord-like line with a wide Spread and two LFOs gently moving Formant and Narrow, so the pad seems to sing different vowels in a big room. Change Roll to soften the top and Spread to widen it.

A low drone while Formant is swept slowly across zero, from below the pitch to far above it. The tone folds through a hollow, ghostly moment at the middle of every pass. Try FM Depth with a cable for a more metallic movement.

A random generator jumps Formant on every sixteenth so a short repeating phrase seems to chatter in a different voice each time, over a broken beat. Lock the pattern with Loop on the Random, or change Spread to widen the chatter.
A saw pad passes through the shifter with a tiny positive Fine and strong Feedback at half Mix: the phaser-like sweep never reaches the end, always rising. Flip Fine negative for a falling one.

With Shift at about +30 % of the 200 Hz range and Mix at 100 %, a harmonic pad becomes inharmonic and metallic, and a slow LFO on Shift moves between bell clusters. Fold in Spread for a stereo glitter.

Feedback through a short FB Delay shifts every repeat up by the same amount, so each plucked note spirals upward into a stack of echoes. Change Shift to climb faster or slower, or make it negative to spiral down.
A mono arpeggio on the left input is shifted in opposite directions left and right by Spread at 100 %, so the sound slowly rotates around the head. Change Fine to rotate faster or slower.
Sync on one bar locks the shifter's rate to the song, so a drum loop and bass get a slow, feedback-laden phaser that sweeps once per bar. Try shorter Sync values, or Shift negative.

Four tracks play a kick, snare, hats and a rim: ghost notes, coin-flip hits, ratchets and a little Swing make a loose, breathing beat that changes a bit every loop. Lower a track's Chance, or pick Dice = Fixed, to tighten it.

Four tracks of different Lengths (5, 7, 9 and 11 steps) each strike their own bell in A minor pentatonic, so the chord of bells slowly rearranges itself. Change a Length by one step and the whole weave shifts.

Each track owns a Note (A1, C2, E2, G2) and its own rhythm of hits, ties and ratchets; the Notes output merges them into one bass line that drives a mono voice. Change a track's Note setting to re-tune its part of the line.

Every step of four tracks is armed, and slow LFOs on the Chance knobs decide how many of them fire: glassy D-minor drops thicken into a downpour and thin out again, each track on its own cycle. Turn a Chance knob by hand to hear one track's density.

A four-on-the-floor groove where a slow square LFO holds Fill for the last bar of every four, switching in extra hits and ratchets, and another LFO on Mute 4 drops the percussion for a while. Hold the Fill button yourself, or mute tracks, to arrange it live.

A short plucked phrase is recorded, then a slow square LFO on the Freeze gate holds the buffer for a few bars at a time: the grains turn one moment of the phrase into a wide, endless pad, and the next phrase is caught when the freeze lets go.
Triggered mode with Sync on 1/16: every step fires a short, reversed-or-forward grain of a bass loop, chopping it into a stuttering rhythm. Raise Density to fire bursts.
Pitch Quant on Octaves + fifths and a little Pitch Jitter turn a slow melody into a shimmering halo that climbs by fifths and octaves. Feedback keeps the glow after each note.
A sequencer drives the Pitch input of a frozen noise burst's grains, so the cloud itself plays the tune: a shimmering sine-like melody made of nothing but grains.
Long grains that mostly play backwards, scattered by Spread and Pitch Jitter around a slow melody, with Blur washing everything: a swelling, reversed-reverb garden.

The classic I – vi – IV – V in C major runs as a progression with the transport, four beats per chord. Tone 1 – 4 feed a soft pad and Bass a sine below. Click a slot in the view to change its chord or length, or switch Quality to Diatonic Seventh.

A ii – V – I – VI progression written with fixed roots and rich qualities (minor 9, dominant 9, major 9, dominant 7♭9), one slot with a slash bass. Each change plucks the chord and the Bass output walks underneath, on a shuffle. Edit the qualities in the progression strip.

Advance is set to Trigger: a syncopated step sequencer pulses Next, so the chord changes exactly when you want, cycling through five minor-key chords as short stabs over a pumping root bass. Try Advance Transport to hear it follow the slot lengths instead.

In A minor the progression visits E major, whose G♯ is not in the scale. With Scale Policy on Adapt the published scale bends to A harmonic minor for that chord, so a Quantizer Suite following the bus plays the G♯ in its random pluck line. Switch Scale Policy to Keep and listen to the line lose it.

Manual source: a slow stepped Random walks the Degree knob through the Mixolydian chords while a sequencer on Transpose moves the whole key up a fourth and a fifth every few bars. Each change swells in a warm pad with a root drone below. Try Quality Diatonic Triad or another Scale.

A saw oscillator is pinged by a pentatonic sequence through the gate's Classic cell: each note opens fast and darkens as it dies, like a struck wooden bar. Turn Response for shorter or longer plucks and Resonance for more ring.

patches.name: Low Pass Gate: Slow Memory Bass

preset.description: The Slow memory cell remembers earlier pings, so a sub-heavy bass line opens a little more with each note that follows another quickly. Switch Cell to Fast to hear it forget.
Three gates ping from a Drum Grid: a low sine for the kick, noise for the snare and a bright square for the ticks. Everything is the gate's own pluck envelope; Response sets how tight the drums are.
The gate's Light output, a ready-made pluck envelope, opens a Multi Filter on a drone, so a quiet saw pad brightens with each ping and dims again. Change Response to stretch the glow.

A slow LFO on the CV input opens and closes the gate over a held saw chord, with the Slow memory cell smoothing every swell into a breathing, darker-as-it-closes pad. Lower Brightness or add Resonance to change the colour.

The Pluck model struck by a sequencer trigger rings like a plucked string, and its built-in decay and low-pass gate need no envelope at all. Try a longer Decay for sustain or move Tone for a brighter string.
Three Macro Oscs play a whole drum kit from one grid: the Kick, Snare and Metal models, each struck by its own trigger. Change Tone and Decay on each one to retune the kit.
The Chord model plays a whole chord from one pitch; slow LFOs on Tone and Shape change the chord type and voicing, and Aux carries a second voice to the other side. Turn Blend to taste.
The Phase Warp model with an envelope on its Tone macro: each bass note starts wide open and bent, then settles into a round, quiet sound. Try other Models such as Fold or FM on the same line.

The Dust model scatters tiny pitched clicks, with the sequencer walking them through a pentatonic scale, and a second Macro Oscillator on Noise Band adds airy breath beneath. Move Tone for denser crackle and Blend for a wider texture.

Eight inputs, four outputs: a lead, a bass and a drum kit go in, outputs 3 and 4 are sends to an echo and a reverb, and their returns come back into the matrix to be mixed into the main left and right. Each crosspoint is a send amount - try the lead's 1 -> 3 and 1 -> 4 circles.

Two stored snapshots: A is a sparse scene (lead left, bass centre, pad), B a full groove with drums and the lead on the right. A slow LFO on Morph blends smoothly between them, so the arrangement keeps changing by itself. Click a snapshot button to hear it alone, or drag Morph.

Every crosspoint is also a knob, so an audio-rate oscillator patched into the 1 -> 1 gain turns the matrix into a ring modulator: the left output is the metallic product, the right output the dry melody. A slow LFO detunes the modulator for sweeping bell tones. Try changing the 1 -> 2 crosspoint to blend dry and ring.

Two echo networks sit between matrix outputs and inputs, and their returns feed one another through the crosspoints with Normalize on, so the loops build a glassy web of repeats that never runs away. Lower or raise the crosspoint gains around 0.5 to thin out or thicken the web.

The matrix isn't only for audio: four slow Quad LFO waves go in, and four differently blended mixes (some inverted) come out to move the filter of each voice of a chord. Change the crosspoint signs to make voices open when others close.

A plain sine melody is the carrier; with nothing patched into Modulator the internal oscillator ring-modulates it, and a slow LFO sweeps Osc Tune so the plucks turn into shifting, inharmonic bells. Try Timbre towards 100 % to let the carrier bleed through, or change Osc Octave.

The vocoder algorithm lets a drum beat talk through a sustained buzzy chord: every kick, snare and hat from the Modulator carves its rhythm and spectrum into the Carrier. Move Timbre to shift the formants, or change Algorithm to hear the same signals ring-modulated.

Algorithm 7 (Chebyshev) turns a pure sine into its Nth harmonic, and a stepped Random picks N for every sixteenth: the same note blurs through brighter and brighter overtones like an arpeggio inside each pitch. Turn Timbre by hand to hear single harmonics, or raise Carrier Level for a hotter sound.

A bass voice made entirely inside Meta Mod: a sequencer plays its internal oscillator while a second oscillator a fifth up goes into Modulator, and a slow LFO glides Algorithm between ring, crossfade and fold. Listen for the growl when the algorithm passes the ring-mod area, then change Timbre.

Algorithm 4 treats the carrier and modulator as integers and combines their bits: a saw lead and a square arpeggio turn into gritty, digital chords. A slow LFO lowers and raises Timbre (the bit resolution); switch Bitwise Op between XOR, AND, OR and Sum mod for different textures.

Mallet strikes on a wooden bar: a quick pentatonic phrase played by the Strike input, with Geometry at the bar setting and a short, damped ring. Strike Timbre changes the mallet from soft to hard, Position moves where on the bar it lands.

Long held gates with Bow turned up make the string sing continuously, with a slow rise of bow pressure from a Triangle LFO. Lower Bow Timbre for a softer scrape, or raise Damping to shorten the sustain.
Blow, not bow or strike: breath noise excites a tube-like body and a slow melody speaks out of it with a soft, airy attack. Blow Timbre sets the colour of the air, Geometry the shape of the body.

Hits on a big metal plate in a rhythmic pattern, with slow LFOs morphing Geometry between string, plate and bell and sweeping Brightness. Try Size, Damping and Space for a tighter or a more cavernous plate.

patches.name: Modal Voice: Drums Through a Body

preset.description: A drum beat enters the Ext input and excites the modal body, so the kit rings like it is played on a tuned bell with a bass line from the sequencer's pitch. Ext Level is the amount of beat in the body; Coarse retunes the whole thing.

Neuron A fires regularly from its own bias; as it charges, its Out pushes Neuron B down, so B fires in irregular gaps. A Spike plays the kick, B Spike the snare and A AND B a clap over a pad: a rhythm made by two cells listening to each other. Try the Leak knobs or the W3 weights.

Neuron A's spikes ping a pair of low pass gates, while Neuron B's saw-like Out is sampled by a quantizer on every spike: pitches from an irregular rhythm, in D minor pentatonic, through a long delay. Change the Pulse and Leak of either neuron to rewrite the tune.

A slow triangle LFO feeds Neuron A's In 2: the higher it rises, the faster A fires, so the hats and rim accelerate into a roll and fall silent as the level drops. Neuron B answers with a tom. Try a different W2 or Threshold to move where the roll starts.

With Leak near 0 and Cross on Gate, the two neurons chase each other so fast that their output is an audio-rate buzz. A slow LFO bends the weights and so the pitch, a filter tames it and a slow envelope shapes it into a drifting, electric drone. Nudge W3 or Pulse to retune it.

Both neurons are in Compare mode, each a Schmitt trigger on its own clocked LFO. Their gates are combined by AND, OR and XOR into kick, clap and hats, so a few slow waves yield a changing polymetric groove. Change the Threshold of A or B to change which crossings count.

Eight slow, related LFOs move a four-note chord: four of them open and close the filters, four more shift each voice's waveform, and the level of each voice drifts too. Raise Drift or Spread in the view and the pad starts to breathe unevenly.

Lock is on Bars, so LFO 1 breathes once every two bars and the other seven float loosely around the song. They open the filter of a plucked line and pan its echoes while a light beat keeps time. Try Anchor off or a higher Drift to let it slip out of step.

Max follows whichever of the eight LFOs is highest and drives the cutoff of a saw arpeggio, so the sound flares open every time one of them peaks. The Sum output slowly widens the reverb. Turn Twist up for sharper flares and Scatter down to make them line up.
Four sawtooth voices on one note are each detuned by their own LFO, running at a lively 0.6 Hz with high Drift: a restless, chorusing swarm. Try a negative Spread to slow the LFOs down along the row.

Four bell-like tones, each gated by its own fast, sharp-peaked Organic LFO (Twist +1, Unipolar): irregular pulses fall like rain and never repeat. Move Rate or Spread to make the shower faster or more uneven.

Three Perc Voices make a whole kit: an FM kick with a long Sweep, a snappy mid voice with plenty of Click, and a hat from the Noise Bank engine. Change a voice's Tone or Decay to move between boom, tom and metal.

With Track on, the sequencer's pitch tunes the Modal engine, so a membrane voice plays a melodic line like a set of tuned toms. Decay and Damp set how much the notes ring into each other; Sweep gives each hit its dive.

Tone near the top of its range and the FM engine turn the voice into a long, inharmonic bell; a slow sparse line plays it, with a second quieter bell an octave higher. Try Morph and Spread for different bell colours.

Two Noise Bank voices play off-beat shakers and a rim-like tick, with random accents so no two bars are alike. Pitch sets the colour of the bank, Decay the length of the shake, and Damp how fast the highs die.

One voice plays the same rhythm while a slow LFO walks Tone from pure sine through membrane and bar to metal, then back: a single hit becomes a kick, a tom, a wood block and a clang over time. Switch Engine to hear the same sweep three ways.

Rhythm 16, notes 5, octaves 7, gates 12 and chances 9 steps long: each track loops at its own length, so the soft A major pentatonic figure only repeats after hundreds of steps. Change one track's length in the view and the pattern re-weaves itself.

An E Phrygian Dominant bass line from tracks of 13, 7, 5 and 11 steps, with ties for slides and a few ratchets, over a four-on-the-floor beat. Move Prob. Bias or Ratchet Amt to thin the line out or make it stutter.

Each track runs at its own Division: triggers at double speed, notes at normal speed, octaves at half speed, gates ping-ponging and probability in thirds. A bright marimba line in D Dorian that keeps changing shape. Try other divisions on the tracks.

Three stored patterns with different track lengths share one voice. A slow saw LFO on the Pattern input moves from slot to slot on the next bar, so the tune changes character every few bars. Click a slot in the view to hear it alone.

Sparse, probability-driven bursts of high notes over a slow drone: ratchets turn single notes into showers, and a slow LFO on Prob. Bias keeps the density rising and falling. Turn Ratchet Amt down for plain notes, or up for more rain.

A Pulse Generator synced to 1/16 is the clock for a melody, while a second one rings a short pulse into hi-hat ticks. Jitter on the first one loosens the groove; try it at 0 for a rigid machine and at 40 % for a drunk one.

A very short pulse struck once per note makes the Ring resonance ping, and the sequencer's pitch moves Ring Freq, so each note is a glassy, metallic chime. Turn Damping to change how long they ring, or Width to change their colour.

Four Pulse Generators in Triggered mode, each struck by a Drum Grid track: Ring Freq and Damping turn the same circuit into a deep thump, a tom, a rim click and a hat. Change their Ring Freq and Damping for a whole new kit.

Burst fires four to eight pulses 30 ms apart for a drum roll, and Double adds a second pulse for a flam. A sparse beat triggers them, so the kit rolls in at the ends of phrases. Try Burst 16 or a longer Period.

In External Width mode the Pulse Generator is a gate delay: each gate of a slow melody comes out 330 ms later, as long as it went in, and opens a second voice an octave up. Change Delay to move the echo, and Width to see the gate length.

In Quadrature mode four sines run a quarter cycle apart. Out 1 and Out 2 pan two plucked lines in a slow circle around the listener while the other two outputs swell a pad. Switch the module's view to XY to see the circle, and change Rate 1 to spin it faster.

Divide mode runs four falling saws at x1, 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 of one rate, each plucking a note of an A minor chord: a 4-against-3-against-2 pattern that only lines up every twelve beats. Change Divide 2-4 to remix the polyrhythm.

Phase mode with Spread at 90 degrees lets four unipolar sines pass one swell along the voices of a major-seventh chord: the chord rolls up and down like a breath. Try Spread 0 (all together) or 180 (two pairs).

The Cycle outputs fire once per LFO cycle, and in Divide mode each LFO has its own fraction of the rate: kick every beat, hat every half beat, clap every third and a tom every fifth - a drum pattern that slowly phases. Change the Divide settings to rearrange it.

A sequencer's step trigger is patched into Clock: LFO 1 runs one cycle per Clock Ratio pulses, here two, and a square wave chops a sustained saw chord on that grid while LFO 2 sweeps the filter. Change Clock Ratio or Pulse Width to change the rhythm of the chop.

A stepped Random would wander through every note; the Quantizer Suite's note mask keeps only the five pentatonic notes of D major, so any value lands somewhere beautiful. Channel B quantizes the same notes an octave down for a bass. Click notes on and off on the keyboard in the view.

One E Dorian melody goes into In A only; the unpatched inputs inherit it, and channels B, C and D transpose it by 2, 4 and 7 scale steps, so a single line turns into a moving four-part chord. Change the Steps knobs to reshape the harmony.

Channels A and B in Arp mode build a seventh chord and a random triad on each slow root and play them as sixteenth-note arpeggios, one up and down over two octaves, one shuffled an octave higher. Try another Order or Chord, or Span 3.

Four channels follow a Harmony Master on bus A. A random contour is snapped to the nearest chord tone for a lead, a second channel adds the chord tone two steps above, and a third in Root mode makes a bass line from the same contour. Change a channel's Target to Scale or Chord + Scale.

A smooth random curve is quantized to F Lydian and held by Track & Hold, with Slew gliding between the notes; channel B follows a fifth up (Steps +4) with a longer slew. Two singing lines that slide from note to note. Raise a Slew knob for slower glides.

T Mode Drums turns the T section into a kick (T1) and a snare (T2) that favour beats 1 and 3, 2 and 4, with occasional ghost notes. X, snapped to F minor pentatonic and clocked by the kicks, plays the bass. T Recall at 60 % keeps the figure recognisable while it changes; try 0 % or 100 %.

With T Recall and X Recall at 100 % the random gates and notes are locked into an eight-step loop, a ready-made melody in A minor pentatonic. Because the memory holds raw random numbers, changing the Scale, X Spread or X Bias reshapes the same contour. Lower the Recall knobs to let it mutate again.

T Mode Ratchet lets every tick fire as divisions or as two to four quick pulses: T1 rattles a hi-hat, T2 a clap, over a steady kick and a pulsing bass. T Bias towards the right gives more ratchets, towards the left sparse divisions. Try Gate Length and T Jitter.

X Mode Sorted makes X1, X2 and X3 always low, middle and high, so three soft voices drift through a D major pentatonic chord that changes every half note; T chance gates re-swell them. Spread sets how wide the chord is, Bias how high it sits.

A slow LFO moves both Recall knobs from always-new to a locked loop and back, while T Loop is 5 and X Loop 7 so the rhythm and the melody never line up. The D Dorian pluck line crystallises, mutates, and crystallises again; a bass follows the second gate. Try setting the Recall knobs by hand.

The Modal model rings like a bell or plate each time a sequencer strums it, tuned by the Pitch input. Structure moves from string to bar to bell, Damping decides how long they ring, and Position changes which overtones are struck.

The String model with four voices turns a running arpeggio into a harp: each trigger plucks a string that rings over the next. Brightness and Damping change the string, Position moves the pluck point toward the bridge.

A soft saw melody is fed into the Sympathetic model, whose strings ring along with whatever matches them: the tune turns into a shimmering sitar-like cloud. Try Frequency (in semitones) to retune the strings against the melody.

A drum beat is the exciter: Strum Source is set to Input onsets, so every kick, snare and hat hit makes the tuned body ring a note of a slow, random-walking bass line. Turn Dry up for the plain kit, or Structure for a different resonant body.

Rhythmic bursts of filtered noise strike a plate whose Structure and Brightness drift on slow LFOs, so the metallic timbre keeps changing from rubbed glass to gong. Change the strum rate, Damping or Position to retune the surface.

A slow, soft melody disappears into a huge room: Size and Decay are high, Damping rolls the tail dark, and Pre-delay keeps each note clear before the bloom. Try Decay and Size together, or push Mix to 100 %.
A drum beat in a small, dry room: low Size, a short Decay and high Damping glue the kit together like a booth. Raise Size and Decay to move the same beat into a hall.

A square LFO opens the Freeze gate for a couple of bars at a time, holding whatever is in the tank as an endless chord, then lets it go so the next phrase can be caught. Edit the LFO's Sync, or latch Freeze yourself.

Slow LFOs ride Size and Decay while Mod Depth swirls the tail, so the room itself seems to inhale and exhale around a gentle arpeggio. Every Verb knob modulates click-free: try patching your own LFO into Tone.

Pre-delay is locked to a dotted eighth, so a bright plucked tune is followed by one clear rhythmic echo and then a short, diffuse bloom. Change Pre-delay Sync, or lower Diffusion to hear the individual reflections.

In the Even family the four outputs spread different numbers of hits evenly over 16 steps: kick, snare, hats and rim lock into a lopsided but steady groove. Turn Pattern to browse related grooves or use Rotate 1-4 to shift one drum against the others.

With Family on Prime and Length on Open the four parts repeat every few steps (2, 3, 5, 7 ...) and slowly drift against each other, each plucking a different note of a minor pentatonic scale, so the melody never repeats the same way twice. Try other Pattern numbers for different cycle lengths.

The Metric family builds a kit by metric weight: kick on the one, snare on the backbeat, hats on the off-beats. A Random steps Pattern once per bar, so the groove changes bar by bar but always from the same family. Try Complement on Avoid to stop the parts from colliding.

The Poly family plays between 2 and 9 hits per cycle across the same bar, not tied to the sixteenths: with Grid on Free the hits land at their exact positions on four hand drums and a bell. Switch Grid to Snap to hear them squared up.

Interlock never lets two parts hit on the same step, and Complement on Fill makes Out 4 play every step the other three leave empty: kick, snare and rim weave around a continuous ride of hats. Try Rotate 1-4 or Pattern to reshuffle who plays where.

Eight integer divisions of the 16th-note clock (/1 to /8) strike a hat, tom, kick, rim, clap and cowbell, forming polyrhythms that realign every four bars. A slow ramp on Rotate shifts which drum gets which division at each bar; turn Rotate by hand and listen to the kit re-gear.

The Primes set (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17) on eighth notes strikes six bells of an F major-pentatonic chord, so the chimes drift through patterns that almost never repeat. A slow ramp on Rotate hands the fast and slow divisions to different bells over time.

Gate output on quarter notes with the Fibonacci set (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34): each division opens one note of a C major-nine chord, so the pad breathes in and out as the gates fall in and out of step. Widen or narrow Width to change how long each note is held.

Powers of 2 split the 16th clock into a clean techno grid: /1 hats, /2 off-beat accents, /4 kick, /8 clap, /16 a bar-long ping. The Stair output counts how many divisions fire together and, snapped to a scale, plays the bass: busier beats climb higher.

Set = Custom with the divisions 4, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12 drives a tuned drum ensemble of toms, a rim, a cowbell, a hat and a clap: a kit that lines up only every few bars (Realign sets 8). Type other numbers into the divisions in the view for a new meter.

Five segments draw an envelope no ADSR can: a bright attack, a quick drop, a second bloom, a held sustain and a slow release. The same shape opens the VCA and the filter. Drag the points in the graph, or turn Time 3 and Level 3 to move the second bloom.

Run on Free with Sync turns four looped segments into a tempo-locked LFO of a shape no standard wave has: a fast curved rise, a dip and two uneven steps. It sweeps the filter on a bass line. Drag the points or change the note values to reshape the wobble.

Eight Step segments on Free with Sync at 1/8 are a tiny sequencer: each segment's Level is a pitch, and a Quantizer snaps the staircase to A minor pentatonic. Drag the Levels in the graph to write a new tune, or change Count to shorten the loop.

A long chord is shaped by a swell of two peaks: it rises, dips and rises again before holding while the gate is high, then releases slowly. Time Scale stretches the whole breath at once; try it, or move the dip's Level.

Eight looped Step segments of an eighth note each make a one-bar clock: every segment's gate output fires a drum, so the Seg outputs are a patchable pattern, while the stepped Out moves a bass filter. Try patching other Seg outputs onto other drums.

A Shape Env triggered by every note replaces the ADSR: it plays a Pluck shape in One-shot mode, and a slow LFO on Morph blends it with its neighbours, so the notes slide between snappy and soft plucks. Browse other shapes with the Shape knob while it plays.

A drawn-style gate shape looped over one bar and locked to the song chops a sustained chord into a rhythm, like a trance gate. Change Shape to another of the rhythmic patterns, or sweep Morph to blend between two of them.

Shape Env plays the Echoes 1/8 shape, a burst that repeats itself on the beat grid, once per trigger from a slow melody, so every bell note comes back as a row of echoes without any delay effect. Change Sync or Skew to move the echoes, or try Ping-pong or Bounce 5.

The Breathing shape loops every four seconds and opens and closes a low-pass filter on a sustained chord, while Inv, the upside-down shape, moves a second filter band the opposite way. Try other Wobbles shapes or change Time for a slower or faster breath.

Five Shape Envs build the drums from sine oscillators: Short exp as pitch drop and Pluck as amplitude make a kick and a tom, and the Roll shape fills out a snare of noise. Change Time or the shapes to retune and reshape each drum.

An eight-bit register in E minor pentatonic with Lock almost at 100 %: the melody repeats, and a very slow LFO lets it slip a note now and then before it settles again. Pull Lock down by hand to loosen it, or push it to the top to freeze the tune.

One sixteen-step pattern in the register, read at four places: the kick takes Bit 1, the clap Bit 3, the hats Bit 4 and a rim Bit 6, so the same rhythm echoes itself two, three and five steps later. Lower Lock to let the groove mutate, change Length for new cycles.

Source = Data: a little kick-and-snare pattern is fed into the register's Data input and comes back out of the bits as echoes that drive chimes and a pad of notes. Lock below 100 % corrupts the echoes, so the rhythm slowly drifts from its original.

Lock at -100 % flips every returning bit, so the five-step pattern comes back inverted and the whole line repeats every ten steps. The Combo output (odd number of the chosen bits) rings a high bell, Voltage opens the filter. Move Lock towards the middle to hear the mirror blur.

Sync = Free: the register runs on its own Rate instead of the song tempo, and a slow LFO speeds it up and slows it down, over a whole-tone scale. A second LFO on Lock moves between frozen, mutating and random. Switch Sync to a note value to lock it back to the beat.

One trigger per bar fires all six slopes, but Harmonics spreads their rates so each note of a six-note chord opens a moment after the last: a strum. Turn Harmonics down to bring the notes together, Skew for plucks or swells.

In Loop mode six slopes run slightly apart (Harmonics 0.13), each swelling one chord tone, so the chord's colour drifts as the pulses phase against each other. Nudge Harmonics, Rate or Skew to change the pattern.

Loop mode with Sync on one bar and Snap on Integer runs six slopes at one to six cycles per bar, locked to the song: six pentatonic notes pulsing in a polyrhythm. Try Skew for short blips and Curve for sharper decays.
A six-track grid fires six slopes, one per drum trigger, and each shapes a different sine tone into a synthetic toms-and-blips kit. One set of Skew and Curve knobs shapes all six decays at once.

In Sound mode the six slopes become audio oscillators locked to the sequencer's pitch with Snap on Just: a six-note chord in pure ratios whose spread you change with Harmonics, moved slowly by an LFO.

A plucked phrase is recorded into the reel for one bar, then the splice loops it back, locked to the bars by Sync, and you hear the live phrase pass through while it is recorded. Try Sync, Speed or Window Size to bend the loop.

A short recorded chord arpeggio is chopped into 3 % windows with high Overlap, turning it into a granular cloud that a slow LFO scrubs across the splice via Position. Raise Window Size to hear the phrase re-emerge.

One recorded note is replayed as an instrument: a sequencer's Pitch drives the Speed input (1 V per octave) and its trigger restarts the splice, with Loop on One-shot. Change the sequence, or Window Size, for different timbres.

A drum beat is recorded to the reel, then a stepped random source on Select and a clock on Next hop through its splices and a fast random Position, re-cutting the groove on the fly. Try Shift (Immediate against End of window) and Overlap.

A slow melody is caught on the reel and played back at a speed that a slow LFO sweeps from forward through standstill to reverse, like a tape dragged by hand. Change the LFO's depth or fix Speed at -1 for plain reverse.

Eight stages of C harmonic minor: held notes, repeats, a ratchet and two slides make a one-bar riff, with louder accented stages. Change a stage's Pulses or Gate mode in the view, or raise Slide Time to melt the slides further.

Pendulum mode swings back and forth across six stages of long held notes in F Lydian, each lasting four to eight pulses; a pair of detuned oscillators and a slowly opening filter turn the chord-like line into a pad. Change Mode to Forward or Reverse, or shorten the Pulses.

Brownian mode takes one stage up or down at a time, so the sixteen-stage bell melody in D major pentatonic wanders like a drunk on a staircase and always returns to the same neighbours. Change the Seed, or switch Mode to Random, to hear a different walk.

A reversed run of E minor stages with slides between stages and accents that fire the Accent Gate: it opens the filter with an extra snap on the accented stages. Turn Accent or Slide Time to change the squelch, or add pulses to a stage to lengthen it.

Random mode with a two-bar Phrase: ten A Dorian stages come in a shuffled order that repeats every phrase. A square LFO on the Hold input freezes the sequence on one stage for a bar, and the Stage output sweeps the filter. Try a longer Phrase, or hold Hold yourself.

A slow LFO on Spread opens the swarm from a single note into a full Minor 9 chord and closes it again, while the Spread output also opens a filter, so the pad blooms and fades. Try other Chord entries or a higher Count.

A low swarm on the Cluster chord with strong Drift and a little Cross FM: dozens of close-packed pitches beat against each other into a restless, ominous drone. Lower Spread to tighten it, or raise Cross FM for a grittier texture.

The swarm spread over a Major Pentatonic scale with a plucky envelope and Reshuffle fired every bar: each bar the notes rearrange themselves, so the same rhythm rains down in a new order. Try Pattern: Random and a larger Spread.
Seven oscillators on the Octaves chord with a wide Detune make a huge, thick bass that holds together over the beat. Try Fifths or a bigger Range for more weight, or reduce Detune for a cleaner tone.
A bright swarm of stacked fifths with Warp pushed up and Cross FM on a slow cycle: the oscillators modulate each other into a glittering, bell-like shimmer. Move Warp and Cross FM to taste.

A ramp wave sweeps from 100 Hz to 8 kHz in exactly four bars, locked to the song, through a low-pass that opens with it, and End fires a noise crash as it flies back. Change Start, Stop, Law or Sweep Sync to reshape the build.

Two Up-Down triangle sweeps of different lengths, panned apart, wail over a slow bass and drift in and out of phase. Try Law Log for an even siren, Waveform Pulse for a harsher one, or a shorter Sweep Time.

In Burst mode the sweep climbs slowly in silence, and each step of a sequencer plays a short tone burst at whatever frequency it has reached. Over eight bars they rise from 200 Hz to 4 kHz, like a stepped frequency measurement. Try Burst Count or a different Waveform.

Three Sweep Generators of different lengths (one bar, two bars, half a note) each fire a Marker when their Up-Down sweep crosses a set frequency, striking a kick, a snare and a hat: the sweeps play a drifting polyrhythm. Change a Marker frequency or Sweep Sync to move the hits.

Triggered mode with a falling sweep: each note of the sequencer fires one fast zap from high to low, and the note's pitch (the Pitch input) shifts where the sweep starts and ends. Lengthen Sweep Time for slower sirens, or switch Law to Lin.

Three lamp-stabilised sines tuned to a root, a fifth and an octave, each with a long Settle and plenty of Drift: they warm up from flat, swell and bounce against each other, with a slow wobble on one dial. Try Loop Gain between 100 % and 150 %, or Settle at 0.1 s for faster bounces.

With Loop Gain below 100 % the oscillator does not run: it rings when kicked, so each Drum Grid hit becomes a tuned drum, a deep kick on Range ×10, a tom on ×100 and a rim tick on ×1k. Raise Loop Gain towards 100 % for longer rings, or lower Kick for softer hits.

A drum loop goes into Audio In of a test oscillator held just below self-oscillation at 95 %, and a sequencer steers its Pitch: the loop plays a melody through the tuned resonator. Change Loop Gain for a shorter or longer ring, or Frequency for a different key.

A tiny Settle lets the lamp chase the waveform itself, and Loop Gain at 210 % clips it: the sine turns into a squealing, fluttering square-ish tone that stutters between bursts. A bass line steers the pitch; try Settle between 5 and 50 ms and Loop Gain near 150 % for gentler flutter.

A bass line jumps the dial of a lamp-regulated sine: each leap dips the amplitude and it surges back, a living bounce. The Lamp output follows that heat and sweeps the cutoff of a saw lead, so the lead breathes with the bass. Try Settle to change the bounce time.

Tidal in Slow range takes about half a minute per cycle: output A slowly opens the filter on a held chord with a long rise and a quicker fall (Skew), while output B fades the volume in and out. Try Skew and Frequency for a faster or more lopsided tide.

With Relation on Phase and Spread at maximum, outputs A and B are a sine and a cosine of the same slope: they steer two plucked voices around the stereo field in opposite directions. Change Frequency or Curve to speed the circling up or square it off.

One trigger per bar fires Tidal in AD mode with Relation on Harmonic: its four outputs become four envelopes of different lengths, each opening a VCA on a different chord tone, so the chord dissolves note by note. Try Skew, Frequency or Spread to change how the tones fall away.

Range Audio turns Tidal into a voice: a sequencer plays its Pitch input, Skew sweeps saw to triangle, and a slow Smooth fold adds overtones. A and B go to the left and right channels with a little Spread for width. Try Smooth and Skew by hand while it plays.

Tidal locked to the song with Sync 1 bar and Relation on Ratio gives four slopes that meet again only after several bars: they sweep the filter, the pulse shape, the tone of a pad stab and the volume of a bass. Try other Sync values or Ratio to change the cycle.

Quantized 1 jumps between eight levels two semitones apart on every sixteenth, and a quantizer pulls them into D minor pentatonic: a small random vocabulary the ear hears as a tune. Lower Q1 Bits for fewer notes, or change Q1 Interval and Seed for a different melody.

The two Fluctuating outputs are smooth random curves with different speeds: one opens and closes the filters of a four-voice chord, the other pans the voices together and bends their waveform. Nothing repeats. Raise F1 Rate or F2 Rate for a busier shimmer, or lower F1 Spread for a calmer pad.

Stored takes a new value every half note and Correlation keeps each close to the last; Integrated turns that into long random sweeps that open and close the filter of a saw arpeggio. A one-bit Quantized 2 switches the hats on and off. Change Correlation to make the sweeps longer or jitterier.

A fixed riff plays while two Uncertainty quantizers decorate it: Quantized 2 with Interval 12 sends each note to one of four octaves, and a one-bit Quantized 1 on Interval 7 adds a fifth now and then. Try Q2 Bits 1 for a plain octave jump or Q2 Divide /1 for a new octave on every note.

Stored picks a new value on every step and with Correlation at +85 % each is close to the last, so the pitch wanders up and down like a drunken walk; a quantizer keeps it in F Lydian and pinged low pass gates turn each step into a bell. Try Correlation negative for a zig-zag, or the Shape set to Edges.

A narrow band sweeps up five octaves through a low saw drone, lighting up each harmonic in turn: the Band output plays the overtone series as a rising melody, and every harmonic it finds fires Peak, which plays the hats. Try Bandwidth 100 Hz or a faster Sync.

patches.name: Wave Analyzer: One Pitch from Everything

preset.description: A wide-open sweep drifts through a plucked saw melody while Shifted moves whatever partial it finds to the Listen frequency: the tune becomes a stream of changing timbres all at one pitch. Move Listen to change that pitch, or Bandwidth to 3 Hz for purer tones.

In Lock mode the analyser hunts for the loudest partial within Capture of the dial, locks on and follows it: Track drives a square voice an octave below that doubles the melody, and Locked gates it. Widen Capture or move Frequency to change what it grabs.

A slow synced sweep reads a three-saw chord from 20 Hz up through the whole spectrum in four bars; the Band output sings each partial as it passes and the plotter draws the spectrum. Try Hold on a slow LFO to freeze a partial, or Sync Free for a looser sweep.

The sweep moves through a bass-and-lead sequence, but a square LFO on Hold freezes it on one partial for a bar at a time, then lets it run again; the wide 1/3-octave Bandwidth makes the band whistle and talk. Change the Hold rate or Bandwidth to taste.

The Folder's internal sine, played from a sequencer's pitch, is folded harder as an envelope opens Fold: every note starts bright and metallic, then relaxes toward a pure tone. Change Fold, Symmetry or Tap for other timbres.
A low sine from the Folder's own oscillator, with slow LFOs on Symmetry and Tap, turns from hollow to buzzy and back. Raise Fold for more teeth, or turn Octave up for a lead.

An Oscillator patched into the Folder's input frequency-modulates its internal sine through FM Depth, then the result is folded: sparkling, bell-like tones with a quick decay. Raise FM Depth or Fold to turn bells to glass.

An external plucked saw goes into the Folder with a gentle Fold and Mix at half: the folds add upper harmonics to the dry sound, and Spread opens it into stereo. Move Fold and Level to see how far into the folds the signal reaches.
A whole drum loop passes through the Folder: kicks gain harmonics and snare and hats turn crunchy as Fold rises with a slow LFO. Pull Mix back for parallel crunch.

A slow triangle LFO on Scan walks the Analog bank along the Snake path, smoothly blending one cycle into the next, with a little Stereo spread. Try another Bank or Path, or switch Frame Blend to Step for stair-stepped changes.

The Vowel bank with X and Y pushed around by two random generators, so a short tune seems to speak in changing vowels. Set X and Y by hand to pick a single vowel, or lock the Random Loop for a repeating phrase.
Struck notes from the Bell bank with Y moved by the note envelope: each bell starts bright and metallic and fades toward a plain tone. Try a different X position for other bell colours.

A Digital bank bass with Warp in Sync mode, opened on every note by an envelope for a tearing, vocal attack that settles into a solid tone, plus a Sub for weight. Try other Warp Modes such as Mirror or Squash.

A repeating arpeggio in the Spectra bank while Scan crawls along the Spiral path from the middle outward; the X and Y position outputs open a filter, so the table's movement shapes the whole sound. Try Columns or Diagonal paths.

Wobble's Stepped output picks a new pitch every eighth note and a Quantizer keeps them in D Dorian, while the Wobble output opens the filter with a springy overshoot. Raise Chaos to make the tune run in streaks, or lower Smooth for sharper filter jumps.
A bass line goes through a ladder filter whose cutoff is bounced by Wobble's overshooting output, one new value every eighth. Try Wobble at 100 % for wilder rings or Smooth up to soften the jumps.

Wobble's Burst output fires quick rolls of triggers on a quarter-note grid into a tom, while Stepped retunes the tom every step and Compare gates the open hats. Turn Burst up for more rolls and Burst Size for longer ones.

At 0.15 Hz with Smooth at 100 %, Wobble becomes a slow wandering line: Smooth sweeps the filter, Wobble slides the pulse width of two detuned oscillators, Stepped nudges the pitch within a held chord. Try Rate and Chaos for a faster or more restless drift.

A slow triangle LFO is sampled by Wobble on every sixteenth through its Sample input, so the Stepped output draws a rising and falling staircase; a Quantizer turns it into an arpeggio. Change the LFO's Sync, or raise Chaos so the line breaks away from the staircase.

Two sines a few cents apart draw a figure that slowly turns; Phase turns that rotation into a sawtooth LFO that sweeps the filter of a drifting pad, speeding up as the oscillators drift further apart. Watch the loop open and close while the pad opens with it, and try Persistence for longer trails.

A fixed sine on X and a sequenced sine on Y trace the figure of each interval: a line for unison, a figure-eight for the octave, a woven knot for the fifth. Ratio feeds a triangle voice that follows the interval, so the scope also plays the harmony. Try Mode Y-T for the same sound as a waveform.

Two drifting oscillators wander in and out of tune. Whenever the figure stands still the Still gate goes high and opens a melody, so the tune plays only in the moments they agree. Set Still Tolerance to Tight for rarer windows or Loose for more.

The left and right sides of a detuned saw pad go to X and Y, so you see the stereo image: a rounder cloud when the sides drift apart. Correlation controls the cutoff of an arpeggio, so the wider the pad swells, the darker the arpeggio. Change the Detune of the pad to change the picture.

Mode Y-T turns the scope into an oscilloscope: the drum loop is drawn as a waveform, one sweep per beat in Trigger Beat, with the bass on X as a second dimmer trace. Try a shorter Timebase, a longer Persistence or Trigger Y Rising.

Zone 3 locked to the transport gives a warm dotted echo with a tape Character; Ping-Pong from a slow square LFO flips the repeats between a straight tail and a bouncing one. Ride Feedback and Tone to dub it live.

In the Comb zone the delay is tuned by the Pitch input, so a sequencer plays a resonant, string-like ring from short noise-free pulses of a saw. Feedback sets how long each note rings; Character shapes its colour.

Zone 5 is a multi-bar loop: a Hold gate from an LFO freezes the buffer for a few bars, then releases it, while Reverse flips the held phrase. Change Zone or Time to shorten the loop, or hold it by hand.

A stepped random source jumps Time around in Tape mode, so every change bends the echoes up or down in pitch like a tape machine being thrown about. Lower Glide for sharper swoops, or switch Time Change to Crossfade for stepped echoes.

A drum groove runs through a Long-zone delay with full Diffuse and high Feedback: the first echo is clear, then the repeats melt into a reverb-like cloud behind the kit. Reduce Diffuse for distinct repeats, or try Offset for a wider image.
